label: Người thật · Hollywood
text:
PRESET live_action_feature. Hollywood live-action feature-film cinematography; photorealistic imagery with an 8K Ultra HD level of fine detail. Real human anatomy, distinctive faces, natural pores and fine lines, subtle skin colour variation, individual hair strands and believable eyes. Preserve each character’s specified age, identity and proportions. Render fabric weave, leather grain, metal wear, wood fibres and stone with physically believable texture and reflections. Maintain this photographic visual language across all shots and asset references. Avoid waxy skin, beauty-filter smoothing, artificial sharpening, glossy game-like surfaces and digital-painting textures.

Environments should feel like tangible locations and constructed film sets, with coherent scale, practical construction, natural imperfections and believable contact between objects. Follow the project’s established period, architecture, costume and prop rules. Atmospheric and magical effects, when present, should have a clear source, restrained intensity and convincing interaction with nearby surfaces.

For narrative scenes, use motivated daylight, moonlight, windows, practical fixtures or fire appropriate to the setting. Keep faces readable, highlights gently rolled off and shadows detailed; preserve natural skin tones within the scene’s colour palette. Use realistic lens perspective and selective depth of field for emotion, with sufficient depth for geography and important actions. For white-background asset references, use neutral studio lighting, accurate colours and even focus across all required details and views.

For video, use natural live-action timing, believable weight, grounded foot contact and subtle facial performance. Hair, clothing and environmental motion should respond consistently to movement and physical forces. Use shot-motivated camera movement and natural motion blur. Maintain stable identity, anatomy, materials and lighting continuity; avoid morphing, texture crawling and unintended exposure flicker.

label: 2D Nhật hiện đại
text:
PRESET anime_jp_modern. Modern Japanese 2D anime feature-film aesthetic; precise hand-drawn contours, controlled line-weight variation, expressive anime facial construction and clearly designed hair shapes. Preserve each character’s specified age, identity, facial proportions and silhouette. Use clean colour fills with two or three deliberate cel-shading tones and selective graphic highlights. Suggest materials through folds, linework, colour and shadow shapes rather than photographic microtexture. Maintain a consistently drawn 2D appearance across characters, props and effects. Avoid photoreal skin, sculpted CGI faces, glossy 3D shading and unrequested chibi transformations.

Environments should use richly painted anime backgrounds with coherent perspective, selective texture and atmospheric depth. Match background detail and colour design to the characters so both belong to the same scene. Follow the project’s established period, architecture, costumes and props. When present, magical effects should use designed 2D shapes, controlled glow and readable silhouettes without overwhelming the acting.

For narrative scenes, translate motivated light sources into clear cel-shadow shapes, deliberate colour relationships and restrained compositing. Keep eyes, expressions and silhouettes legible. Establish depth primarily through staging, overlap, scale and atmospheric perspective; use selective background softness sparingly. For white-background asset references, use clean model-sheet presentation, neutral colours, minimal cel shading and consistent proportions across views.

For video, use a slightly choppy, intentionally stepped anime cadence on a 24 fps timeline: character animation mainly on twos, occasional holds on threes, and selective animation on ones for fast actions or expressive accents. Combine strong key poses, economical in-betweens and purposeful holds with subtle secondary motion. Camera moves may remain smooth independently of held character drawings. Keep linework, facial construction and colour fills stable. Avoid random stuttering, interpolated facial warping and uniformly ultra-smooth motion.

label: 2D Mỹ · Cartoon
text:
PRESET cartoon_us_2d. American theatrical 2D cartoon animation aesthetic; expressive hand-drawn characters, confident flowing contours, clear shape language and strong readable silhouettes. Use appealing stylized proportions, flexible brows and mouths, and facial construction that supports a broad emotional range. Preserve each character’s specified age, identity and established design. Render characters with clean colour fills, economical cel shadows and selective highlights. Describe materials through graphic shapes, folds and purposeful line accents. Maintain a consistently drawn 2D appearance. Avoid photoreal textures, sculpted 3D surfaces and generic stock-vector or clip-art styling.

Environments should use designed, painted backgrounds with coherent perspective, selective brush texture and clear foreground, middle-ground and background separation. Coordinate scenery, props and characters through a shared shape language and colour palette. Follow the project’s established period, architecture, costumes and props. Draw atmospheric and magical effects as readable 2D forms with controlled visual complexity.

For narrative scenes, use clear value grouping, expressive colour design and simplified lighting motivated by sources within the setting. Keep faces, gestures and silhouettes easy to read. Create depth through staging, overlap, scale and multiplane composition, with restrained blur. For white-background asset references, use clean model-sheet presentation, neutral colours, minimal shading and consistent construction across every required view.

For video, use expressive pose-to-pose animation with clear anticipation, rhythmic timing, purposeful squash and stretch, overlapping action and follow-through. Match exaggeration to the scene’s emotion. Use animation on twos where appropriate and ones for fast or fluid passages; allow brief smear drawings during rapid movement. Preserve character volume and return cleanly to the established design after deformations. Avoid mechanical puppet motion, arbitrary jitter, persistent off-model distortion and effects that obscure the performance.
